e-158.problem:
A function $f(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| **$x$** | $0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $1.1$ | $1.3$ | $1.7$ | $2.5$ |

Approximate $f'(x)$ at the point $x=0.2$ using a central difference approximation.
e-158.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x+h) - f(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=0.2.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0.2) & ≈\frac{f(0.2+0.1)-f(0.2-0.1)}{2(0.1)} \\  & =\frac{f(0.3)-f(0.1)}{2(0.1)} \\  & =\frac{1.7-1.1}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{0.6}{0.2} \\  & =\frac{6}{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

e-160.problem:
A car engine is being heated from a temperature of about $-10^{\circ}.$ The temperature of the engine after $t$ minutes is given by $T(t).$  The graph of $T(t)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14059223/assets/fe78a78911e2df9cdb488ec57b0e0a34bb56e18b57303d895dc8013b64a4afc3.png)

Approximate the rate at which the temperature of the engine increases when $t = 3$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
e-160.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
T'(t) \approx \dfrac{T(t+h) - T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 

at the time $t=3$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{T(3+1)-T(3-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{T(4)-T(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{60-30}{2} \\  & =\frac{30}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of temperature increase is approximately $15^{\circ}$ per minute.

The temperature of a certain liquid under heating is given by the function $T(t),$ where $t$ is the time in hours. The values of $T(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.2$ | $1.4$ | $1.6$ | $1.8$ | $2.0$ | $2.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T(t)$ | $-12$ | $-10$ | $-4$ | $6$ | $10$ | $13$ |

$$

$$

Determine the instantaneous temperature rate at the instant of time $t=1.6$ using a central difference approximation with the step size $h=0.2.$
after.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(t)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=1.6$ with step size $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(1.6) & ≈\frac{T(1.6+0.2)-T(1.6-0.2)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{T(1.8)-T(1.4)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{6-(-10)}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{16}{0.4} \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous temperature rate at the instant of time $t=1.6$ is ${40}^{∘}$ per hour.

In a lab experiment, the temperature of a chemical reactor (in ${}^{∘}C$) after $t$ minutes is given by the function $T(t).$ The values of $T(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.2$ | $1.6$ | $2.0$ | $2.4$ | $2.8$ | $3.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$T(t)$** | $28$ | $30$ | $32$ | $34$ | $35$ | $36$ |

Approximate the reactor’s temperature instantaneous rate of change at $t=2.0$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.4.$

The reactor’s temperature at $t=2.0$ is changing at approximately 
{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}C$ per minute.
after.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(t)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=2.0$ with step size $h=0.4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(2.0) & ≈\frac{T(2.0+0.4)-T(2.0-0.4)}{2(0.4)} \\  & =\frac{T(2.4)-T(1.6)}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{34-30}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{4}{0.8} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the reactor’s temperature at $t=2.0$ is changing at approximately $5\,{}^{∘}C$ per minute.
